text:
I give you thanks, Love
I give you
        thanks, Love,
for every grief and torment,
and from this day on I am
        content with every pain.
Content am I with all I have been able to suffer,

        Lord, in your beautiful kingdom;
for by your grace, though I deserved nothing,

        you have given me so great a gift,
since you have made me worthy
of so
        blessed a smile,

which has carried my heart to paradise.
I give you thanks,
        Love.
To paradise my heart have carried
the lovely laughing eyes,

        where I saw you, Love, hiding
with your burning flames.

        O lovely shining eyes,
that have stolen my heart!


I give you thanks, Love.
I feared for my life:
My lady
        dressed in white,
with a loving smile, came joyfully
to my aid, beautiful and
        honest:
her head was adorned
with roses and wallflowers,
and her
        eyes outshine the sun in their splendor.
I give you thanks, Love.

        Version by Carlos López Narváez

translation.title: Ballad V
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish rendering, identified as a version by Carlos López Narváez, rather than directly from the Italian original; the refrain, shifted lineation, and devotional address are preserved. The supplied body opens with a standalone repetition of the refrain before its next line, and that duplicate opening is retained.
